decision: Use dry-run-first, atomic file replacement with post-write verification and symlink refusal for qrexec lab deployment artifacts.

approaches.name: atomic verified installer
approaches.correctness: high: exact content and mode are checked after install
approaches.robustness: high: temp-file rename, idempotency, symlink/non-file refusal
approaches.regressionRisk: low: separate deployment primitive; no runtime protocol changes
approaches.qa: dry-run, idempotency, drift detection, permissions, symlink refusal

approaches.name: blind shell copy/chmod
approaches.robustness: low: weak verification and partial-write handling
approaches.regressionRisk: medium: deployment drift can go unnoticed

approaches.name: package-manager installation
approaches.regressionRisk: high for current lab stage due to packaging surface
approaches.qa: requires packaging/repository CI not yet present

approaches.name: configuration-management agent
approaches.resourceUse: high relative to two-file lab install
approaches.regressionRisk: medium-high: adds another privileged control plane
approaches.qa: strong but disproportionate for current scope

lessons: Deployment verification must treat content drift and permission drift as failures.
Installer output should report hashes and paths, never worker secret material.
Existing symlink targets are refused to avoid redirecting privileged writes.
Dry-run is the default so a Qubes operator can inspect the exact plan before applying it.
Secret rotation remains a separate gate because safe revocation also requires worker re-enrollment/counter semantics and coordinator lifecycle handling.
safetyScope: Synthetic defensive Qubes lab orchestration only; no financial transactions, exploitation, stolen payment data, or weakened security controls.
